rows.title: Lamont’s commitment to CT’s fiscal ‘guardrails’ is being tested
rows.standfirst: Vanishing ARPA funds will test Gov. Ned Lamont’s commitment to budget ‘guardrails’ as lawmakers seek more funds for Medicaid and education.

rows.title: Lamont to propose $54M increase in special education funding
rows.standfirst: The budget proposal will include a $40 million increase in special education funding and a $14 million grant to develop in-district programs.

rows.title: CT Senate GOP: Cut income tax, freeze state employee wages
rows.standfirst: In addition to a state employee wage freeze and income tax cut, CT Republicans want to cap municipal property tax increases at 2%.

rows.title: Lamont works around CT budget ‘guardrails’ to back child care
rows.standfirst: In addition to investing in child care, Gov. Ned Lamont’s $55.2 billion, two-year budget proposal will include a $50 income tax cut.

rows.title: Lamont proposes loosening guardrails, boosting child care in $55.2B budget
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s proposed $55.2B budget would reform CT’s ‘fiscal guardrails’ and launch a major early childhood development initiative.

rows.title: How much would your town get under Lamont’s proposed budget?
rows.standfirst: Some towns would gain and some would lose state funding under Gov. Ned Lamont’s proposal for town aid grants for the next two fiscal years.

rows.title: Lamont’s business tax changes would hit film and TV companies, large corporations
rows.standfirst: The changes would raise revenue from large, multistate corporations and limit a tax credit that has fostered movie and television production.

rows.title: Child care is center of governor’s human services budget
rows.standfirst: Lamont’s budget invests in universal preschool but does not meet the needs of other nonprofits, like food banks and homelessness providers.

rows.title: Lamont’s offer to reform CT budget ‘guardrails’ pleases Democrats
rows.standfirst: While Gov. Ned Lamont didn’t move the ‘fiscal guardrails’ as far as some of his fellow Democrats had hoped, the overture was appreciated.

rows.title: Lamont wants to dip into opioid settlement to fund social services
rows.standfirst: Despite a CT law ensuring the money would be used to counteract the epidemic, Lamont wants to tap into it to pay for social service programs.

rows.title: CT budget: What’s in Lamont’s $55.2B proposal?
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont unveiled a $55.2 billion biennial CT budget on Wednesday. Here’s what it would mean for several areas of state funding.

rows.title: Lamont budget calls for CT to ramp up transportation projects
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s budget would keep CT on pace to dramatically accelerate the rebuilding of its aging highways, bridges and rail lines.

rows.title: Analysts: CT is paying off pension debt faster than all other states
rows.standfirst: CT paid down pension debt faster than the rest of the nation in 2022 and continues to outpace most states, analysts told lawmakers Tuesday.

rows.title: CT Democrats’ special education plan faces funding challenge
rows.standfirst: CT Democrats want $40 million more in special education grants this year and say they’ll find cuts to make it work within the spending cap.

rows.title: Lamont calls legislature’s special education plan fiscally ‘irresponsible’
rows.standfirst: The special education plan would push CT’s budget $100 million over spending cap, said a strongly opposed Gov. Ned Lamont.

rows.title: CT’s dilemma: Cut aid to some schools to boost help for others?
rows.standfirst: Rural towns say they’re unfairly penalized under the state’s ECS formula, which would cut aid to 80 municipalities in the proposed budget.

rows.title: CT’s spending cap battle was years in the making
rows.standfirst: With pandemic aid nearly gone, CT officials’ efforts to re-embrace the spending cap is coming at the worst possible time for many.
